The **Tyler County Fairgrounds** is a location in The Forest region of Appalachia in *Fallout 76*. [Pub 1] 

Sitting at the convergence of State Routes 81 and 90, the attraction served as a tourist destination before the Great War. Features included a 100-foot tall Ferris Wheel, a classic carousel, rides, concessions, crafts, arcade games, and a livestock show and auction. [1] [2] 

““All the fun of the fair” has been replaced by “all the salivating horror of the Scorched.” This large area of rusting fairgrounds is a great place to find uncommon items and search for health as you secure the nearby Tyler County Dirt Track (Public Workshop). Don’t overlook the mechanic’s 
warehouse either—a must-visit if you’re a fan of pumpkin displays”— Atlas of Appalachia

The Tyler County Fairgrounds is a large grassy area across State Route 81 from the Tyler County Dirt Track. A series of celebratory attractions were slated for the "Tyler County Scare!" Halloween event, the decorations of which can still be found around the location. [3] [4] 

The rides at the park include Rally Rollers, the Rocket Whirl, a carousel, and Ferris wheel. Other attractions include Jar Toss (the roof of which is inhabited by Liebowitz), Hole in One, Nothing but Net and Bandit Roundup. There are also arcade games such as Atomic Rollers, Whac-a-Commie, and Hoop Shot. An Ammunition Vending Machine is located next to the Bandit Roundup booth.

The prize booth is located on the western side of the fairgrounds near the Bandit Roundup booth and contains several toys. A tall stand in the shape of a giant Nuka-Cola bottle can be found in the center of the grounds. Inside the stand are free Nuka-Cola samples as well as a First Aid. Approximately 30 Mason Jars can be found at the Jar Toss booth.

There is a Cooking Station in the Funnel Fun concession stand. A shed in the makeshift parking lot to the west has a sign advertising the "Tyler County Scare!" Inside is a Tinker's Workbench and Halloween display, complete with Pumpkins, candy, and orange and black decorations.

- Funnel Fun
- Hole in One
- Throw and Bowl
- Nothing But Net
- Farm to Food
- Jar Toss
- Bandit Roundup
- Rally Rollers
- Rocket Whirl
- Carousel
- Ferris Wheel

- My story - Note, on the roof of the Farm To Food booth. Before *Wastelanders* , it was placed on the Jar Toss booth.
- Three potential Vault-Tec Bobbleheads:
 - Inside the "Tyler County Scare" building near the front, on the long table.
 - In the Nuka-Cola stand that is shaped like a giant bottle, on the metal shelving.
 - On the south side of the fairgrounds, in the room with three "Hoop Shots" games, on a token dispenser.
- Three potential Magazines:
 - In the long metal barn near the large slide, on top of one of the two wooden barrels.
 - Inside the prize booth with the green and white top, sitting on a shelf with a Toy Rocketship.
 - On the east side of the arcade, near the "Apples, Hotdogs" stall, inside a portable toilet.
- Potential Weapon Mod - On a crate, inside the middle of the green trailer in the middle of the fairgrounds.
- Potential Recipe - At the eastern end of the area, in the Funnel Fun Funnel Cake stand, on a shelf.
- At least one of every type of Teddy Bear that can be found in the game, if one wishes to display the entire collection at their C.A.M.P.

This location is one of three amusement parks in Appalachia, the other being Camden Park and Wavy Willard's Water Park.

Tyler County Fairgrounds appears in *Fallout 76*.

- The Tyler County Fairgrounds are based on the real-world location of the same name, located adjacent to the Tyler County Speedway in Middlebourne, West Virginia.
- Steve Massey worked on the location's design. [Dev 1]
